task.description:
Gate CODE-DESIGNER's amendment to `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md`, commit `c756b82` on `feature/WF03-ISS0193-20260821`. This design closes ISS-0193, which is ITSELF a finding from this same design's own PRIOR gate (WF03-ISS0119-20260821 Step 4e) -- the shape mechanism got the closed-and-pinned rule then and it worked; the vocabulary mechanism (A5) did not, and that gap is what you are now checking was actually closed, not merely described as closed. Read the producer's own report in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0193-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json` `result`, then re-derive from the diff -- don't trust the summary.

RE-DERIVE, each item names what to check yourself:

1. THE NEW A5 RULE. Open the new §13.6 (or wherever it landed) and confirm it states, unambiguously and independent of set equality: every `known_anomalies:` record's `path:` must name a volume whose index entry has `status: closed` AND a `frozen_prefix_sha256:`. Compare its exact wording against A4b's §13.5 text side by side -- confirm it is a correct mirror (same enforcement strength, same failure independence), not a weaker paraphrase.

2. THE THREE EXISTING RECORDS -- CHECK THE FILE YOURSELF. Open `docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml` directly. Confirm each of the three `known_anomalies:` records' `path:` and the cited volume's `status:`/`frozen_prefix_sha256:` fields, at the exact line numbers the design claims (74/81/88 for the records; 32-52, specifically 34/46, for the volume entry). Do not accept the producer's line citations without opening the file and reading them yourself -- a wrong citation here would mean the fix is unverified against its own only real-world test case.

3. THE A10 SHARED ASSERTION -- THE PART MOST LIKELY TO HIDE A SOFT SPOT. `warranted_closure?(volume, max_lines, max_bytes) :: boolean()` is supposed to prevent the laundering route your own predecessor gate found (MINOR-4 on WF03-ISS0119-20260821: closing a volume in the same commit as a declaration passes every existing check because nothing asserts the roll was warranted). Confirm the design specifies EXACTLY what 'actually exceeded at closure' compares -- the index's recorded `lines:`/`bytes_working_tree:` snapshot at closure time, not a live re-measurement (a live re-measurement would be meaningless once later volumes exist) -- and confirm it is genuinely SHARED (both A4b and the new A5 rule call the same function) rather than reimplemented twice with a chance to diverge. Stress-test it mentally against the exact laundering scenario MINOR-4 described: does A10, as specified, actually block it now? Walk through the scenario step by step and state the walk-through in your result.

4. VOLUME 1 COMPATIBILITY. Confirm from the index file directly that volume 1's `lines: 5766` / `bytes_working_tree: 361376` exceeds `roll_rule.max_lines: 1200` / `max_bytes: 120000` (or whatever the actual current roll_rule values are -- read them, don't assume the numbers in this dispatch are current). A10 must not retroactively fail the one closed volume that exists.

5. SECTION 13.3's RECONCILED WORDING. Read it in its new form and confirm it reads as settled fact with an ISS-0193 citation, not left as a stale forward-looking caveat and not silently deleted.

6. NO WEAKENING. Confirm A5's bidirectional set-equality property is untouched, and the three existing `known_anomalies:` records are untouched (not edited, not deleted, not renumbered).

7. TEST/SUPPORT SPECIFICATION IS ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTABLE. Read the test/support-file specification section. Could TEST-DESIGNER and ELIXIR-DEV implement `warranted_closure?/3`, the renamed `closed_pinned_and_warranted?/3`, the A10 test, and the negative-control fixtures directly from what is written, without having to invent a missing detail? Name any gap.

8. DESIGN-ARTEFACT DISCIPLINE. Confirm no `.ex` implementation body was written -- signatures, type shapes and assertion prose only, per this project's standing design-artefact rule.

9. SCOPE. `git show --stat c756b82`: only `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md` and this run's own handoff should appear.

SCOPE OF `result.issues`: only genuine defects -- something that fails a criterion, would let a fresh violation still be laundered, contradicts the file's own established convention, or would leave TEST-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV unable to implement without guessing. Not style or wording preference.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL against the seven acceptance criteria on the Step 02 handoff plus the items above. A FAIL names each failed criterion and the specific gap, and if it concerns A10, states precisely how the laundering route would still succeed against the design as written. Commit your own handoff file to this branch. Do not write `registry.json` or `orchestrator.log`.
acceptance_criteria: The new A5 rule's wording is compared side-by-side against A4b's and confirmed to be an equally strong mirror, not a weaker paraphrase

All three existing known_anomalies: records and volume 1's status/frozen_prefix_sha256 fields were read directly from docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml at the cited line numbers, not accepted from the design's citation

A10's exact comparison basis (index-recorded closure-time snapshot, not live re-measurement) is confirmed, its sharing between A4b and A5 is confirmed (not reimplemented twice), and a step-by-step walkthrough confirms it actually blocks the MINOR-4 laundering scenario
Volume 1's recorded lines/bytes are confirmed, from the index file directly, to exceed the current roll_rule ceiling, so A10 does not retroactively fail it
Section 13.3's reconciled wording is read in its new form and confirmed settled-fact with an ISS-0193 citation
A5's bidirectional set equality and the three existing records are confirmed untouched
The test/support-file specification is confirmed directly implementable, with any gap named
No .ex implementation body is present -- signatures, type shapes and assertion prose only
git show --stat confirms scope is limited to the design file and this run's own handoff
result.issues contains only genuine defects, not stylistic observations

result.summary: Re-derived from the artefact itself, not from CODE-DESIGNER's summary. All 10 acceptance criteria met. (1) A5's new rule (design.md's new §13.6 paragraph beginning 'A5 additionally asserts') is a verbatim mirror of A4b's §13.5 rule with only 'known_shape_anomalies:' swapped for 'known_anomalies:' -- identical enforcement strength, same independence from set equality ('independently of set equality, and even when the on-disk violation it cites genuinely exists' appears in both). (2) Opened docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml directly: the three known_anomalies: record '- path:' lines are at exactly lines 74, 81, 88, all citing docs/status/requirement_status.yaml; volume 1's entry spans lines 32-52, with status: closed at line 34 and frozen_prefix_sha256 at line 46 -- all citations in the design and in CODE-DESIGNER's summary check out exactly. (3) A10 walkthrough: MINOR-4's scenario is closing a volume EARLY (before it genuinely reaches roll_rule ceiling) in the same commit that declares a record against it, so that A1/A2/A6/A7/A8 and the closed-and-pinned rule all pass on 'a correctly-performed roll.' A10 as specified reads the index's own recorded lines:/bytes_working_tree: snapshot (not a live re-measurement) and requires it to exceed roll_rule.max_lines or max_bytes; an honestly-recorded early closure has small numbers that do not exceed the ceiling, so warranted_closure?/3 returns false, closed_pinned_and_warranted?/3 returns false, and the record fails A4b/A5 with reason :not_warranted. This does block the MINOR-4 scenario exactly as described. Sharing confirmed: both A4b's and A5's closed-and-pinned findings call the single renamed closed_pinned_and_warranted?/3 helper, which delegates the roll-rule comparison to one shared StatusHistory.warranted_closure?/3 -- verified test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs already has closed_and_pinned?/2 at line 510 (to be renamed) called only from A4b's findings (line 490), matching the design's premise. Also verified test/support/status_history.ex's real parse_index/1 (already on disk) generically parses every 4-space-indented field under a volumes: list item via parse_list/put_field, so it already returns :lines and :bytes_working_tree per volume despite not being named in section 7's formal type shape -- confirming section 13.12.5's claim that 'parse_index/1's return shape is unchanged... already carries lines:, bytes_working_tree:' is empirically true, not an unverified assumption (this was checked directly against the .ex file, not accepted from the design's say-so). (4) Volume 1: lines: 5766 > roll_rule.max_lines: 1200, and bytes_working_tree: 361376 > roll_rule.max_bytes: 120000 (both read directly from the index, lines 21-22 and 38-39) -- A10 does not retroactively fail the one existing closed volume. (5) Section 13.3's second bullet under 'Why (i), on the merits' was read in its new form: it now states the parity claim 'was written as a forward-looking claim, not yet a fully accurate one' at the time A4b had the rule and A5 didn't, cites ISS-0193 by name, and states 'as of that fix this sentence reads as settled fact rather than aspiration' -- settled-fact framing with citation, not a stale caveat, not silently deleted. (6) A5's bidirectional set-equality property text is untouched from its original wording; all three known_anomalies: records are byte-identical to before (verified against the index file: same lines, same values, same cause text). (7) Test/support spec is directly implementable: warranted_closure?/3's signature, return-value logic, and error-vs-false distinction (raise via Map.fetch! on a closed volume missing lines/bytes, vs. false for a non-closed one) are fully specified; closed_pinned_and_warranted?/3's rename and new roll_rule parameter, its one call site update, the new disqualifying_reason/3 helper, the A10 test placement (after A9), and the two required negative-control fixtures (one closed+pinned+unwarranted volume) are all named concretely with no invented detail required. (8) No .ex implementation bodies present -- the Map.get/Map.fetch! comparisons in section 13.12.4 are inline assertion prose describing exact boolean conditions (consistent with this same artefact's already-gated section 8 reference-implementation convention), not def/end code blocks. (9) git show --stat c756b82 touches exactly two files: lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md and handoffs/WF03-ISS0193-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json -- both in scope, nothing else. (10) issues below is limited to one genuine, non-blocking finding; no stylistic notes included. One MINOR incidental finding recorded: A10 compares against the index's *recorded* lines:/bytes_working_tree: fields for a closed volume, and nothing in this design (or in the current parse_index/1, which parses these generically and trusts whatever text is in the YAML) cross-checks those recorded numbers against a live measurement (StatusHistory.measure/1) of the actual closed file. This does not weaken A10 against the literal MINOR-4 scenario (an honest early closure naturally records small, truthful numbers, which A10 correctly flags as unwarranted) -- but a more sophisticated variant remains open in principle: an agent could fabricate inflated lines:/bytes_working_tree: values in the same commit that closes a volume early, without the file itself being that large, and A10 would read the fabricated numbers as 'exceeded ceiling' with nothing to catch the lie (A6's digest only pins frozen_prefix_lines-worth of content against frozen_prefix_sha256, and does not assert lines:/bytes_working_tree: equal a live measurement of the file). This is a distinct, narrower attack surface than MINOR-4 itself, judged MINOR for the same reason MINOR-4 was: it demands an additional deliberate act (fabricating two numeric fields) beyond an honest roll, and it was not part of the scenario this fix's own dispatch asked to close. Recommend filing as its own incidental issue (a future 'A10-prime': assert a closed volume's recorded lines:/bytes_working_tree: match live StatusHistory.measure/1 of the file, or note why closed-volume immutability makes this unnecessary) rather than reworking this pass.

issues.finding: A10 (design.md section 13.12.4) trusts the index's recorded lines:/bytes_working_tree: fields for a closed volume as the truth of 'size at closure', with no assertion anywhere (A1/A6/A10 included) that those recorded numbers equal a live StatusHistory.measure/1 of the actual closed file. A6's digest only covers the first frozen_prefix_lines lines' content, not whether the separately-declared lines:/bytes_working_tree: fields are truthful. This leaves a narrower, still-open laundering variant: fabricate inflated lines:/bytes_working_tree: values in the same commit that closes a volume early (without the file really being that large), and A10 reads the lie as 'exceeded ceiling.' This does not fail this design's own acceptance criteria -- A10 as specified does block the MINOR-4 scenario exactly as described (an honest early closure) -- but is worth filing as its own incidental finding, the same way MINOR-4 itself was filed out of an already-gated pass rather than reworked in place.

result.next_action: PASS -- route to ELIXIR-DEV (2a)/TEST-DESIGNER per WF-03's issue-resolution path to implement section 13.12's spec (test/support/status_history.ex and test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs changes) against docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml as designed. Recommend ORCH also file the MINOR finding above (A10-prime: no live-measurement cross-check for closed-volume size fields) as its own incidental issue per ISSUE_QUEUE.md, not as rework on this pass.
